display.purpose: The icebreaker prompt only, set in white on the deep-blue masthead. One per page.

title.purpose: Roster names at rest — the words the room reads through compressed video.

body.purpose: Prose: empty-state copy, the completion callout, the demo-bar title.

caption.purpose: Secondary information: the masthead meta line, demo-bar note, footnotes.

label.purpose: Small roles: count labels, toggle text, host pill, left tag.

label-strong.purpose: Button text, primary and ghost alike.

label-loud.purpose: The up-next tag only — the system's one uppercase string.

numeric.purpose: The three big counts, set in deep-blue with tabular figures.

numeric-row.purpose: The standing position number on an ordinary roster row.

numeric-emphasis.purpose: The position number on the up-next row only.

numeric-caption.purpose: The joined-at timestamp; first thing dropped below 640px.

shadows.name: prompt-pinned
shadows.purpose: The system's only box-shadow. Announces that the sticky prompt band has detached from normal flow and pinned to the viewport top; transitions in from 0 4px 16px rgba(0,32,51,0) over 140ms.

motion.name: glide
motion.purpose: Every state transition and most animations: hover, focus, toggle, border, drop-indicator, row-position glide, the completion gesture's three beats, the live-dot pulse, the callout settle.

motion.name: spring
motion.purpose: Reserved for exactly two celebration animations tied to the baton arriving: tag-pop and pos-cue. Nothing else uses it.

motion.name: t-fast
motion.purpose: Default duration for hover, focus, toggle, border, and drop-indicator transitions.

motion.name: t-medium
motion.purpose: Row transform duration; matches the JS-driven FLIP reorder glide in app.js exactly.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The Add button and every other primary action. Deep-blue fill, white text.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font-family: inherit; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.04em; padding: 10px 16px; border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid var(--deep-blue, #005581); background: var(--deep-blue, #005581); color: #ffffff; cursor: pointer; transition: background 140ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), border-color 140ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--deep-blue-hover, #0069a0); border-color: var(--deep-blue-hover, #0069a0); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--deep-blue, #005581); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Secondary actions: Randomize order, Reset session, Exit demo.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { font-family: inherit; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.04em; padding: 10px 16px; border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid var(--hairline, #c9dcea); background: var(--card, #ffffff); color: var(--dim-ink, #1e3e4f); cursor: pointer; transition: background 140ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), color 140ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), border-color 140ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: var(--surface, #e3eef7); color: var(--ink, #002033); border-color: var(--soft-line, #9ec1d9); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--deep-blue, #005581); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Introduced Toggle
components.description: The host's primary per-person interaction. Shown at rest; add .on for the introduced state (deep-blue fill, white text).
components.css: .ds-toggle { font-family: inherit; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.04em; padding: 8px 14px; border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid var(--hairline, #c9dcea); background: var(--card, #ffffff); color: var(--muted-ink, #44616f); cursor: pointer; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; transition: background 140ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), color 140ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), border-color 140ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-toggle:hover { border-color: var(--soft-line, #9ec1d9); color: var(--ink, #002033); } .ds-toggle.on { background: var(--deep-blue, #005581); color: #ffffff; border-color: var(--deep-blue, #005581); } .ds-toggle:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--deep-blue, #005581); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Up-Next Roster Row
components.description: The signature component. The baton lands on this row: gold wash, 2px deep-blue frame, enlarged type — three signals at once, never hue alone.
components.html:
3
Priya Shahyou’re up next
components.css: .ds-row-upnext { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 14px; background: var(--gold-wash, #fff3ce); border: 2px solid var(--deep-blue, #005581); border-radius: 10px; padding: 17px; } .ds-pos { font-family: "Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono", ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 1.5rem; font-weight: 700; color: var(--deep-blue, #005581); font-feature-settings: 'tnum' 1; } .ds-name { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 10px; font-size: 1.25rem; font-weight: 700; color: var(--ink, #002033); } .ds-tag { font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.05em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink, #002033); background: var(--gold, #ffb511); padding: 3px 9px; border-radius: 6px; }

components.name: Completion Callout
components.description: The one whole-room celebration, shown when everyone present has introduced themselves. Wears the gold wash; arrives with a one-shot 1200ms settle.
components.html: Everyone has introduced themselves — that’s the whole room. Enjoy the meeting!
components.css: .ds-callout { background: var(--gold-wash, #fff3ce); border-radius: 10px; padding: 14px 20px; font-size: 0.9375rem; line-height: 1.5; color: var(--ink, #002033); }

components.name: Demo-Mode Bar
components.description: Makes sample data unmistakable. The one border in the system that isn't hairline, soft-line, or deep-blue.

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Add-someone field. Border answers the 3:1 non-text floor since the field has no label of its own to lean on.
components.html: <input class="ds-input" type="text" placeholder="Add someone by name…" />
components.css: .ds-input { font-family: inherit; font-size: 0.9375rem; color: var(--ink, #002033); background: var(--card, #ffffff); border: 1px solid var(--hint-ink, #5b7a8c); padding: 10px 14px; border-radius: 6px; transition: border-color 140ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: var(--muted-ink, #44616f); } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--deep-blue, #005581); }

components.name: Text Link
components.description: The third emphasis level. Re-offers the demo after first run.

components.name: Masthead Live Meta
components.description: The live-status line on the full-bleed deep-blue masthead: a gold dot with a composited pulse halo, plus sky-text meta.
components.css: .ds-meta { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 14px; font-size: 0.8125rem; color: var(--sky-text, #9adcf9); background: var(--deep-blue, #005581); padding: 10px 16px; border-radius: 6px; } .ds-dot { position: relative; width: 7px; height: 7px; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--gold, #ffb511); } .ds-dot::after { content: ""; position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: inherit; background: var(--gold, #ffb511); opacity: 0.45; animation: ds-pulse 2.4s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) infinite; } @keyframes ds-pulse { 0% { transform: scale(1); opacity: 0.45; } 70%, 100% { transform: scale(3.6); opacity: 0; } }

narrative.overview:
A round-robin tracker rebuilt as a clear California day. One deep-blue masthead — the band that holds the live indicator and the icebreaker prompt — bleeds full-width across the top of the page and owns every primary control below it. Gold appears nowhere as decoration; it exists for exactly one job, marking whoever holds the baton right now: the up-next row, the completion callout, the demo-mode bar, text selection. Everything else on the page is sky-tinted blue-on-white, calm enough to sit in the corner of a meeting without competing with the conversation in the room.

This system explicitly retires two prior worlds rather than blending with either: the beige-ledger warm-paper system it replaced (clay accent, paper neutrals, no blue at all), and the navy-dashboard reflex the category defaults to. Neither survives in any token here. The palette is airy and blue rather than warm and paper-toned; the accent is a genuine gold rather than a clay terracotta; and for the first time the system gives its primary color — deep blue — a full-bleed structural role (the masthead) rather than confining it to small controls.

State is still never read through hue alone. Introduced vs. waiting pairs a fill change with an ink-color shift and a checkmark icon; up-next pairs a wash, a 2px deep-blue frame, and larger type, three signals at once. Motion carries exactly two curves: a glide that moves every piece of state, and a spring reserved for precisely two celebration animations. The design wants the room to find the next speaker in one glance and the host to never wonder what a color means.
keyCharacteristics: Sky-tinted ground (#f4f9fd), never gray, never warm paper
Full-bleed deep-blue masthead owns the live indicator, the prompt, and every primary button
Gold is reserved for happy moments only: up-next, completion, demo mode, selection — never a default UI color
Single sans family (Atkinson Hyperlegible Next), single mono (Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono) for numerics, both self-hosted
One functional shadow in the entire stylesheet (the pinned prompt band); everything else is flat
Two motion curves: glide for all state, spring for exactly two one-shot celebrations
No dark theme, ever — the page ships color-scheme: only light specifically to stop browsers from force-inverting it
Screen-share legibility at 720p is the design's first audience

rules.name: The Glide-Everywhere, Spring-Once Rule
rules.body: If it isn't tag-pop or pos-cue, it moves on glide. A third animation reaching for spring needs a reason as strong as "the baton just landed here".

rules.name: The Sequenced-Not-Simultaneous Rule
rules.body: Marking someone introduced fires three beats in order, not at once: background settle, then checkmark draw, then — only if a new person becomes up-next — their position number and tag, delayed to 1800ms and scoped with :has(.just-introduced).

rules.name: The Gold-Under-Ink Rule
rules.body: Gold never carries text on a light ground by itself. It is either a surface that ink sits on top of, or a mark against deep blue — never the text color itself against a light background.

rules.name: The No-Hue-Alone Rule
rules.body: Introduced vs. waiting vs. up-next is never read through color alone. Each state pairs a fill change with an ink-color shift and an icon, or a wash with a border and a size change.

rules.name: Blue Owns the Structure, Gold Owns the Moment
rules.body: Deep blue is the default state of every primary control and the masthead field, present at rest. Gold only appears in response to something happening. A new element with nothing to celebrate reaches for deep blue or a neutral, never gold.

rules.name: The Three-Ink Floor Rule
rules.body: Text answers to exactly three inks depending on role: ink and dim-ink anywhere, muted-ink for secondary text, hint-ink only for a graphical control glyph or where the 3:1 floor applies. Hairline and soft-line are borders only.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next plus Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono is the entire type system. No serif, no second sans, no icon font carrying glyph weight.

rules.name: The Tabular Numerics Rule
rules.body: Every number that updates live renders in Atkinson Mono with font-feature-settings: 'tnum' 1. Numbers must not reflow their container.

rules.name: The Self-Hosted Type Rule
rules.body: Both faces ship from fonts/ as the latin subset, preloaded from index.html, and are never fetched from a CDN.

rules.name: The Screen-Share Floor Rule
rules.body: Body type never goes below 15px; labels never go below 12px. Test by downsampling a screenshot to 1280x720 and reading it from 2m away.

rules.name: The One Uppercase Rule
rules.body: Exactly one string in the system is uppercase: the up-next tag, also the single heaviest label weight (700) in the scale.

rules.name: The Counts-Are-a-Band Rule
rules.body: The three counts render as one continuous flex row on a shared baseline, never as three separate tiles — a direct rejection of PRODUCT.md's named hero-metric-tile anti-reference.

rules.name: The One Breakpoint Rule
rules.body: The system has exactly one breakpoint: 640px. Above it, one layout flexes; below it, the same layout drops columns.

rules.name: The Row-Never-Wraps Rule
rules.body: A roster row stays one line at every width. Below 640px, the timestamp and the up-next tag are both dropped simultaneously so the row keeps its shape; the name never shrinks below Title size.

rules.name: The One Functional Shadow Rule
rules.body: The system's only shadow exists to announce that the sticky prompt band has detached from normal flow. It is not decorative and does not appear anywhere else.

rules.name: The No-Decorative-Glow Rule
rules.body: Backdrop blurs, ambient bloom, hover glows: none survive a screen-share, so none are in the system.

rules.name: The Two-Radius Rule
rules.body: Containers get 10px, controls get 6px. The pill is reserved for annotations and dots.

rules.name: The Border Escalation Rule
rules.body: Reach for border color before background color when marking attention: hairline to soft-line to deep-blue is the fixed ladder. Up-next skips straight to deep-blue at 2px because it is the page's single most important signal.

dos: Do use Ground (#f4f9fd) for the canvas and Card (#ffffff) for content surfaces; Surface (#e3eef7) is the only second tonal layer.
Do carry introduced-vs-waiting-vs-up-next through at least two non-hue signals together: fill + ink color + icon, or wash + border + size.
Do treat gold as a response to something happening, never a resting-state color. Deep blue is what the page looks like when nothing has happened yet.
Do keep every state transition on --glide. Reserve --spring for tag-pop and pos-cue only.
Do render every live-updating number in Atkinson Mono with tabular figures.
Do drop the timestamp and the up-next tag together below 640px; the name never shrinks below Title size.
Do zero animation delays as well as durations under reduced motion, and pin any animation whose meaning lives in its end state explicitly rather than trusting fill-mode.
Do test every screen downsampled to 1280x720, read from 2m away.
donts: Don't ship a dark theme. color-scheme: only light is set specifically to stop the browser from force-inverting the palette.
Don't use gold as a default UI color on any surface that isn't tied to a happy moment (up-next, completion, demo mode, selection).
Don't set text in hairline or soft-line — they are border-only colors (1.4:1 and 1.8:1).
Don't reach for --bright-blue; it is declared but unused in the shipped stylesheet. Give it a real role before treating it as part of the working palette.
Don't put a warning color, countdown, or shaming microcopy on anyone still "to go." PRODUCT.md's no-spotlight-on-absence principle forbids it.
Don't reach for the generic SaaS dashboard idioms PRODUCT.md names by name: hero-metric tiles, identical icon+heading+text card grids, a navy-and-indigo reflex palette.
Don't introduce gamified-leaderboard chrome: avatars, points, badges, celebration animations tied to speed.
Don't mimic Zoom or Slack chrome. The page is shared inside Zoom; it should feel like a separate artifact.
Don't add a second breakpoint, a third border-escalation color, or a third motion curve.
Don't add a shadow anywhere but the pinned prompt band without first asking whether it's signaling something or just decorating.
